topics.title: A 7-year car loan: what the low monthly payment really costs you
topics.angle: The same $40,000 car on a 48-month and an 84-month loan at the same 7% APR: what the lower payment buys, what it costs in interest, and why the long loan usually costs more than that
topics.why_now: Edmunds reports a record 25.5% of financed new cars in Q3 2026 were on loans of 84 months or longer, with the average APR around 7% and an average payment of $787. Dealers sell the monthly number; almost nobody shows the total. A decision people are in right now, evergreen, US (USD), computable with two emi plans. For 22-40 viewers buying their first or second car.
outline: hook: Rohan at the dealer, two payment offers on screen: $958 a month or $604 a month for the same car. He picks the smaller one. Frame one shows both numbers
Priya: 'Same car, same rate. Before you sign, ask one question: how many payments?' (promise line by 25 s: the total cost, the hidden catch, and the one question to ask)
chapter: the two loans. 48 payments of $958 against 84 payments of $604, as two stacks of payment slips side by side
the reveal: total paid $45,977 vs $50,711. The long loan costs $10,711 in interest, nearly twice the $5,977 on the short one
picture the whole video hangs on: a car on a road with a loan balance trailing behind it like a chain. On the long loan the chain is still attached years after the new-car smell is gone
Sharma has seen it before: 'In my bank days, the 84-month buyer came back in year four wanting a new car, and still owed on the old one'

the catch in words (no number unless a maths kind computes it): cars lose value fastest in the first years, so on a long loan you can owe more than the car is worth. Trading it in rolls that debt into the next loan
chapter: the rate is rarely the same. Longer loans usually carry a higher APR: at 8.5% for 84 months the interest becomes $13,211 (emi at 8.5%). Reveal at about two thirds
Rohan: 'So the cheap payment was never cheap.' Sikka cheers the turn
chapter: what to do. 1) ask for the total cost, not the payment; 2) compare 48 and 60 months at the same price; 3) if only the 84-month payment fits, the car may be too expensive
side by side recap: two roads, two totals, one question
end: disclaimer, CTA 'Ask the dealer: how many payments?'
